meta.title: Coupang: The Customers Came Back. Who Decides What They Pay For?
meta.dek: Revenue grew 11% in the quarter the fire, the fines and the margin all landed together. The stock is 53% off its high. What does $15 assume about the margin, and how much of it does Korea's regulator get to keep?
meta.price_note: Nov 3, 2026 regular close (pre-print), Yahoo chart API; the overnight session showed about $14.54
meta.type: Vertically integrated e-commerce: Korean 1P retail, WOW membership, logistics

verdict.sentence: The customers are back and Q3 landed on guidance, but the cash, the Taiwan bill and the regulator all moved the wrong way, and at $15.23 the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle: Watch.
verdict.breaks_if: The regulator reaches the operating model rather than the cash balance: a KFTC order that separates the Eats benefit from WOW or caps how Coupang shares coupon and price-match costs with suppliers removes the mechanism the mid-2027 margin recovery depends on.
verdict.price_implies: between the Base and the Bull (≈$24.5 by 2031 for 10%/yr)

call: Coupang printed the quarter it guided to: revenue of $9.96B, up 11% in constant currency against a guide of 8–9%, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 1.2%, down 329 bps against a guide of 300–400. The customers are the good news. Korean WOW membership is at a record, the members who left have come back to their old spending, and Taiwan's WOW base doubled. The stock closed at $15.23 into the print, 53% below its high, and the PW return is [[pw_return]] a year, not the 13% a holder needs. The cash is why. Trailing free cash flow is $(409)M, the $750M revolver draw is repaid, but the company bought back $1.05B in nine months and net cash fell to $3.68B. The Developing Offerings loss guide went up again, and the October KFTC hearings on Eats and WOW put a remedy on the table that could split the membership bundle. Management says Q3 is the low point and Product Commerce margins return to pre-incident levels by mid-2027. I accept the date and price it in at an 8.5% terminal margin, half a point short. What the market has right is the multiple: ≈16× FY2025 EBITDA already prices recovery. What it has too little of is the order from Seoul. The verb is not probability-fragile; the number that settles it is the KFTC decision on WOW.

tests.claim: That the KFTC fight stays a fine.
tests.test: The KFTC decisions on the Eats merchant-terms case and the WOW tying case (hearings were held in October; fines of up to ₩360B were reported possible in Q4 2026, with the rest by H1 2027), plus the large-retail and dominance probes. A purely monetary sanction passes. A corrective order that separates the Eats benefit from WOW or caps cost-sharing with suppliers, or criminal charges against Coupang Corp., fails.
tests.if_fail: 15 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **Watch / Hold**, entry ≤[[test1.entry]], and the Bear becomes the working case for the margin.

tests.claim: That margin returns with the volume.
tests.test: Product Commerce segment adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 8.0% in the Q2 2027 results (early August 2027), against 9.0% before the incident and 4.6% in Q3 2026. The interim check is the Q4 2026 consolidated margin inside the guided 1.7–2.7% in the late-February release.
tests.if_fail: 10 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **Watch / Hold**, entry ≤[[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That the buyback is paid for by the business.
tests.test: Net cash (cash less all borrowings, leases excluded) of at least $3.0B at the FY2026 10-K (February 2027) and at the Q1 2027 10-Q, with no revolver draw while trailing free cash flow is at or below zero. It was $3.68B on September 30, after the $750M revolver draw was repaid in September.
tests.if_fail: The Base buyback goes to zero and the Outsider grade drops from Outsider-leaning to Reinvestor (PW EV about $18.6, 4.1%/yr, entry about $10.1) → **Watch / Hold**.

return_math.price_implied: At 10% a year the stock must reach about $24.5 by 2031 (15.23 × 1.10^5), which sits between the Base and the Bull. Even with no Bear at all, the Base-and-Bull mix is worth less than that before the optionality line.
return_math.epv: Earnings power today is negative on reported numbers. On FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of ≈$1.5B, less ≈$0.5B of stock pay and ≈$0.5B of depreciation, about $0.5B of pre-tax earnings power capitalized at 12× gives ≈$6B against a $27B market value, so roughly four-fifths of the price pays for recovery and growth `[Estimate]`.
return_math.base_rate: Revenue of ≈$37B puts Coupang in the largest size bucket, where about 32% of companies sustain at least 5% real growth for five years and about 14% reach 10% ([`compounding.md`](../../frameworks/compounding.md)). The Base's ≈9% nominal (about 6–7% real) is a top-quarter outcome and the Bull's ≈11% sits near the 14%. Tiers: Bull plausible, Base probable, Bear probable.
return_math.terminal_growth: On EPS, the 24× and 26× exits imply perpetual growth of about 5.6% and 5.9% at a 10% discount rate, above the 4.9% Treasury, so the multiples lean on growth continuing past 2031. The Base is still growing about 9% in FY2031, which the Taiwan lever has to supply. The Bear's $7.5 is set on EBITDA, not EPS.
return_math.year_ten: The Base is still growing mid-single digits at year ten on online penetration, attach and Taiwan, against a population that peaks around 2030, so the terminal multiple is not doing all the work.
return_math.rr_note: The downside is a regulatory order, not a weak quarter: the Bear sits about half below spot.
return_math.note: Computed rows come from model.json. The Bear's terminal value is set outside the engine at 8× FY2031 adjusted EBITDA plus ≈$2.5B of net cash because its earnings are near zero. EPV, base rate and year ten are the author's. Built with Claude.
